from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Biot's Law models this rotation.", "Rotation is proportional to concentration.", "Increased concentration compresses the Barber Pole stripes."]
        self.setup_layout("Mathematical Model: Biot's Law", lecture_lines)
        
        # Math objects
        biot_eq = MathTex(r"\theta = [\alpha] \cdot c \cdot L", font_size=40)
        self.place_at_grid(biot_eq, "B2")

        # Barber Pole simulation
        beaker = Rectangle(height=3, width=1, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(beaker, "D4")
        
        # Stripes
        stripes = VGroup(*[Line(start=[-0.5, y, 0], end=[0.5, y, 0], color=BLUE) for y in np.linspace(-1.4, 1.4, 10)])
        stripes.rotate(PI/4)
        stripes.move_to(beaker.get_center())
        self.add(stripes)

        # Concentration variable
        c = ValueTracker(1.0)
        
        def update_stripes(s):
            new_stripes = VGroup(*[Line(start=[-0.5, y, 0], end=[0.5, y, 0], color=BLUE) for y in np.linspace(-1.4/c.get_value(), 1.4/c.get_value(), 10)])
            new_stripes.rotate(PI/4)
            new_stripes.move_to(beaker.get_center())
            s.become(new_stripes)

        stripes.add_updater(update_stripes)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(biot_eq))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(Indicate(biot_eq), run_time=1)
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(c.animate.set_value(3.0), run_time=3)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        self.wait(1)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Application: The Saccharimeter", [
            "Saccharimeters measure light rotation for purity.",
            "They detect sugar concentration in industrial syrup.",
            "This ensures consistent quality control."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Saccharimeters measure light rotation for purity.
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        # Draw the saccharimeter setup
        source = Dot(color=BLUE).scale(2)
        tube = Rectangle(height=0.5, width=3, color=WHITE, fill_opacity=0.3)
        polarizer = Rectangle(height=1.5, width=0.2, color=GRAY, fill_opacity=0.8)
        
        self.place_at_grid(source, 'C1')
        self.place_at_grid(polarizer, 'C2')
        self.place_at_grid(tube, 'C4')
        
        self.play(FadeIn(source), FadeIn(polarizer), Create(tube))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # They detect sugar concentration in industrial syrup.
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        # Show sugar solution
        solution = Rectangle(height=0.4, width=2.8, color="#E6E6FA", fill_opacity=0.6)
        self.place_at_grid(solution, 'C4')
        self.play(FadeIn(solution))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # This ensures consistent quality control.
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        # Adjust analyzer angle
        analyzer = Rectangle(height=1.5, width=0.2, color=GRAY, fill_opacity=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(analyzer, 'C6')
        self.play(FadeIn(analyzer))
        self.play(Rotate(analyzer, angle=PI/6, about_point=self.grid['C6']))
        
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: The Barber Pole Effect: Polarized Light in Sugar Solutions

sections.title: Prerequisite: Polarization and Malus's Law
sections.content: Briefly define polarized light as a transverse wave oscillating in a single plane. Explain how a polarizer acts as a 'gate' and how passing light through two crossed polarizers results in zero transmission.
sections.example: Visualizing a rope vibrating through a vertical picket fence vs. a horizontal one (blocked).

sections.title: The Mechanism: Optical Activity of Chiral Molecules
sections.content: Introduce 'Optical Activity.' Sugar molecules (sucrose) are chiral, meaning they lack internal symmetry. When light passes through them, the electric field interacts with the electrons in the sugar, causing the plane of polarization to rotate by an angle θ.
sections.example: Representing the sugar molecule as a 'corkscrew' that physically twists the oscillating plane of light as it passes through the solution.

sections.title: The Barber Pole Effect: Spectral Dependence
sections.content: Explain that the rotation angle θ is dependent on the wavelength λ (Rotary Dispersion). Since white light is a mix of colors, each color rotates a different amount. By placing the solution between crossed polarizers, different colors are 'unblocked' at different depths.
sections.example: Graphical animation: A vertical beam entering a beaker; as depth increases, red (long wavelength) rotates slower than blue (short wavelength), creating a vertical column of spiraling rainbow colors—the 'Barber Pole'.

sections.title: Mathematical Model: Biot's Law
sections.content: Introduce the equation θ = [α] * c * L, where [α] is specific rotation, c is concentration, and L is path length. Emphasize that the rotation is linearly proportional to the sugar concentration.
sections.example: A real-time gauge: As sugar is added to the beaker (increasing c), the 'Barber Pole' stripes are shown visually compressing or stretching to illustrate the linear relationship.

sections.title: Application: The Saccharimeter
sections.content: Connect the theory to real-world technology. The 'Saccharimeter' is used in the food industry to measure sugar purity by observing the rotation of light. Discuss how this device serves as a quality control sensor for large-scale syrup production.
sections.example: A virtual lab assistant 'Dr. Sugarcane' using the device to detect if a sample is pure sugar or diluted with water, showcasing industrial precision.
